title: VBL ISR
body:
The **vertical blank** [[ISRs|ISR]]: the interrupt handler that runs once per screen
refresh, fired when the display finishes scanning the last line and before it starts the
next frame. On the Atari ST that is 50 or 60 times a second depending on the video mode.

It is useful because it is the one moment nothing is being drawn to the screen, which
makes it the right place for the [[Double Buffering]] swap. It is also a free, accurate
timebase: a counter incremented in the VBL handler gives you frame timing and animation
pacing without a separate timer chip.

Keep it short. It is an ISR like any other, so it must save and restore context (see
[[Context Switching]]), it runs with the display waiting on it, and anything it shares
with the main loop is a [[Concurrency]] problem. The usual pattern is that the VBL handler
sets a flag or flips a pointer and the main loop does the real work.

One of the three common [[IRQs|IRQ]] sources in this course, alongside the keyboard and
mouse movement.
